t: This is Sloane Avenue, a road in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. It takes its name from Hans Sloane, the Irish-born doctor, botanist and collector. Sloane gathered a collection of some seventy-one thousand items, and when he died in seventeen fifty-three he left it to the British nation. That bequest became the foundation of the British Museum, the British Library and the Natural History Museum. So as you walk along here, you're on a street named for the man whose collection helped start three of London's great institutions.
